entities.summary: Ambelau or Ambalau is a volcanic island in the Banda Sea within Maluku Islands of Indonesia. The island forms an administrative district which is part of the South Buru Regency of Maluku province, Indonesia. It has a land area of 306 km2, and had a population of 6,846 at the 2010 Census; the official estimate as at mid 2023 was 9,225. The administrative center is Wailua, a settlement located at the south of the island. About half of the island's population is composed of indigenous Ambelau people who speak the Ambelau language; the other half are mostly immigrants from the nearby Maluku Islands and Java.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ambalau Island's indigenous population has maintained their unique Ambelau language and culture despite historical influences from neighboring islands. The island's strategic location in the Banda Sea has also made it a significant hub for trade and commerce in Southeast Asia.
